newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND WINS TWO-RUN WORLD CUP DOWNHILL.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND WINS TWO-RUN WORLD CUP DOWNHILL.

text.p: Frenchman Luc Alphand clinched his third victory of the season in a two-run sprint World Cup downhill on Sunday, then admitted he disliked two-leg races.
"To have a sprint downhill once a year is okay but there should definitely not be more such races this winter," said the 31-year-old Alphand.
"A real downhill has to last more than two minutes. It has to have difficult corners and jumps, which this course today did not have.

"Physically, it is a lot easier to race in two runs. Weaker skiers have an advantage because it is all less demanding. A good skier usually wins most of his time over his rivals after a minute, when the muscles start to burn.
"But I won. In two years' time no one will remember that the race I won today was done in two heats. It will simply count as a win on one of the most demanding slopes," he said.
Alphand clocked fastest times in both runs on the shortened version of the usually dreaded Streif piste in Kitzbuehel, for a winning aggregate time of two minutes 12.55 seconds.

The victory marked Alphand's third win on what he has often referred to as his "favourite slope in the world". In 1995, he recorded his maiden World Cup wins here by taking two downhills staged on the same day.
Friday's triumph allowed Alphand to snatch the lead in the downhill World Cup standings from Italian Kristian Ghedina, who finished 11th in 1:13.89. Alphand has 545 points to Ghedina's 489.

"This win does give me confidence for tomorrow's real (full-length) downhill. I know I can be good here this year," said Alphand, who has also won races at the Italian resorts of Val Gardena and Bormio this season.
The Frenchman said he did not put any pressure on himself to do well in Kitzbuehel, as he had done in Chamonix earlier in the month when he finished fifth.
"In Chamonix, I really tried hard because I wanted to win at home," he said. "Today, I just skied the way I always have in the past and it worked."
Austria's Werner Franz held on to his second place after the first leg with a total time of 2:12.95. It was the second time he had finished in second place this winter, after Val D'Isere.
"In Val D'Isere I was really upset about second place because (Austria's Fritz) Strobl beat me by only two-hundredths of a second," said Franz.
"What are two-hundredths? Nothing. You can't say the other guy won because he was better than you. But it is he who walks away with the glory of a victory.
"Today, I'm delighted with second place because Alphand was really the better skier. An advantage of four tenths of a second is quite a lot," added Franz.
Switzerland's William Besse was pleased after improving on a first descent eighth place for overall third in 2:13.13.
"It's great, I am finally finding my form again," said Besse, who had come close to disappearing into ski racing obscurity after disappointing results last season.
Men's World Cup action continues in Kitzbuehel with the classic Hahnenkamm downhill on Saturday and a slalom on Sunday, as well as the season's second combination event.
